issues.legal_issue: Attachment of disputed property under the preventive possession procedure requires a statutory ground, and a mere apprehension of breach of peace does not establish an emergency when the record identifies a party in possession.
material_facts: A police report and the magistrate’s order both recorded that the appellant was in possession of the disputed property and had begun construction there.
The stated grounds for attachment were tension at the site and the possibility that peace could be breached; the record did not explain circumstances establishing an emergency.
A civil suit concerning possession of the property was pending, and the civil court had obtained a local inspection report.
issues.conclusion: The attachment was not justified because no emergency was established; the attachment order and the order affirming it were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 145 and 146(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure form a connected scheme for preventing breaches of peace. Section 145 concerns actual possession, not the merits of a party’s right to possess. Attachment under Section 146(1) is permissible in a case of emergency or where, after the relevant inquiry, the magistrate finds that no party was in possession or cannot determine which party was in possession. Emergency must be distinguished from a mere apprehension of breach of peace, and the magistrate must explain the circumstances and have material on the record supporting that finding. Where the record shows that one party is in possession, attachment cannot be ordered merely on the ground of emergency; the magistrate does not decide whether that possession is lawful. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: attachment_order_review and possession_identified and emergency_material_absent and mere_breach_apprehension

predicates.attachment_order_review: The proceeding is a review of an order attaching disputed property under a preventive procedure concerning possession and public peace.
predicates.possession_identified: The inquiry or order identifies one party as being in actual possession of the disputed property.
predicates.emergency_material_absent: The record contains no material explaining circumstances that establish an emergency requiring attachment.
predicates.mere_breach_apprehension: The stated basis for attachment is only tension or a possibility of a breach of peace.
predicates.civil_suit_pending: A civil proceeding concerning possession of the same property is pending.

issues.definition: When an attachment order is reviewed, one party’s possession is identified, the record lacks material establishing an emergency, and the stated basis is only an apprehension of breach of peace, the attachment is invalid.
